args.title: Use the user's local date, not UTC, in export file names
args.body:
File: src/exportUtils.ts

formatExportFilename builds the date suffix with at.toISOString().slice(0, 10), which always reads the UTC calendar day. For users west of UTC (e.g. Los Angeles), an evening export falls on the next UTC day, so the file name carries tomorrow's date. The date should be derived from the exporting user's local time zone instead of UTC.

args.title: Keep the "(copy)" suffix when truncating a duplicated report's name
args.body:
File: src/api/reports.ts

The duplicate handler builds `${source.name} (copy)` and then truncates the whole string to MAX_NAME_LENGTH, so when the original name is near the limit, truncate() cuts into the appended " (copy)" and replaces the tail with "...", leaving the copy indistinguishable from the original. The name should be truncated first (leaving room for " (copy)") and the suffix appended afterwards, so every duplicate visibly ends in "(copy)".

args.title: Keep non-Latin letters in export file names instead of stripping them
args.body:
File: src/util/strings.ts

slugify() normalizes to NFKD, strips combining marks, then removes anything outside [a-z0-9], which drops Greek, Cyrillic and other non-Latin scripts entirely (while keeping Latin letters once accents are stripped). That leaves every export from such a report named just "report-<date>". slugify should keep letters from any script (e.g. matching on Unicode letter/number classes) rather than only a-z0-9, so distinguishing characters survive into the file name.

args.title: Clear the previous upload error when a new file is chosen
args.body:
File: src/components/UploadForm.tsx

The file input's onChange handler only calls setFile; it never clears the `problem` state from a prior failed upload, so the old error (and row number) stays visible under the form until the user clicks Upload again. The onChange handler should also call setProblem(null) when a new file is picked.

This comment was written by RepoMind, an automated triage agent. To reach a person, mention @ledgerline/maintainers.

Amounts are not floating point: src/util/money.ts stores every amount as an integer number of minor units (cents), parsed by parseAmount() and only converted to a decimal string at display/export time by toMajor()/formatMinor()/formatMoney(). minorDigits() treats currencies without a minor unit (JPY, KRW, VND, CLP, ISK, XAF, XOF) as having 0 decimal digits, so amounts for those are whole integers too, not divided by 100. Nothing needs to change for this report.
